drafted_from: tool row in tools/start-a-computer/tool-rows.json, do-work/start-a-computer.mjs and tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Start a computer on my spare Linux machine at 192.0.2.40 as computer.example.com, with the engine release r1 already on it, and tell me whether the sign-up page answers 200."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a request file, the provider rows in its own read-data/providers.json and the product data you point at, and keeps one lease file.
instructions: 1. Write request.json: lease_file, machine {provider "existing-machine", name, placement {address}, lifetime "service"}, name {host_name}, ssh {known_hosts}, port, engine {file, data_env, data_dir, id_argv, release_name, release}, product_data (the manifest of your product settings) and host_layout. Paths are read relative to the file.

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:start-a-computer"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs start request.json. For a rented machine the provider credential (vault key from the machine row) goes on descriptor 3 and the DNS credential on descriptor 4, never in argv.
3. Read the one JSON line it prints: lease, host_name, arch, price, place_id, release and sign_up_status. If it stops part way, run the same command again: the saved lease resumes it.
4. Run tool:check-a-sign-up against https://<host_name> to prove a new account can sign up, and tool:give-back-a-computer with the lease file when you stop paying for it.

worked_examples.title: A computer started on a machine the person already runs
worked_examples.ask: Start a computer on my spare machine and tell me if the sign-up page answers.
worked_examples.given: From tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs ('starting a computer on an existing machine sets it up, installs the release, serves and reads it back'). request.json = {"lease_file":"lease.json","machine":{"provider":"existing-machine","name":"a-pi","placement":{"address":"192.0.2.40"},"lifetime":"service"},"name":{"host_name":"computer.example.com"},"ssh":{"known_hosts":"known_hosts"},"port":7199,"product_data":"product-data.json","host_layout":{"caddy":{"site_hosts":["computer.example.com"],"port":7199,"releases":"/opt/place/releases"},"units":[{"unit":"place.service","user":"place","releases":"/opt/place/releases","engine_file":"engine","data_env":"ENGINE_DATA","data_dir":"data","config":"/var/lib/place/place.json","launch_setting":"PRODUCT_SETTINGS","product_settings":"/var/lib/place/product-settings.json"}]},"engine":{"file":"engine","data_env":"ENGINE_DATA","data_dir":"data","id_argv":["computer","id"],"release_name":"r1","release":{"on_machine":"/opt/build/release"}}}. The machine reports aarch64 and https://computer.example.com/readyz answers 200. lease_file and the other local paths in a request are read relative to the request file. Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs start request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"lease":{"provider":"existing-machine","name":"a-pi","address":"192.0.2.40","state":"running"},"host_name":"computer.example.com","arch":"aarch64","price":null,"place_id":"ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff","release":"/opt/place/releases/r1","sign_up_status":200}: price is null because no monthly_price_cents was given for a machine the person already runs, and sign_up_status 200 means the public /readyz page answered.
